content.title: 2021 Innovators-In-Residence Program kicks off
content.summary: Aga Khan University's Media Innovation Centre announces three winners of  $20,000 grant

content.text: Three media start-ups from Kenya, Uganda and Tanzania will receive Ksh 9.6million in form of grants and stipends after emerging top of the Aga Khan University Media Innovation Center (MiC), Innovators-in-Residence program selection process.
Making her remarks during the online kick-off event, MiC Director Dr Njoki Chege, said the teams will join the residency program for 12 months.

"After a very stiff and tight selection process, we are happy to announce our three winners today; The Brazen Universe media start-up from Kenya, Minority Africa media start-up from Uganda and Ona Stories media start-up from Tanzania. The three teams will each receive a grant of Ksh 2 million and a monthly stipend of Ksh 100,000 that will go towards developing their start-ups. This will be accompanied by a shared working space in their home countries as well as expert coaching, training and mentorship to help them develop their start-ups," said Dr Chege.
The three start-ups will be hosted at their home country cancelling the need to relocate to Kenya for the residency.

"The MiC has partnered with Media Challenge Initiative (MCI), a Ugandan media hub and Tanzania Media Foundation (TMF). The two teams will experience the same level of coaching and mentorship as if they were having the residency program in Kenya. The partnership with the two media hubs will help us spread our impact regionally and ensure that media start-ups in the two countries receive the support they need."
Dr Chege similarly mentioned the need for grants to fund media start-ups calling for support from international organizations.

"We were amazed at the number of applications received this year. 250 brilliant media start-ups applied for this program with the aim of getting, not only grant funding, but also the coaching and mentorship sessions we offer. This is an indication of a great need for funding in this region and I would like to thank our funders, KfW for making it possible to support these three start-ups. I would therefore like to call upon international organizations and foundations to be a part of the growth of media start-ups in East Africa through our MiC," said Dr Chege.
AKU's Graduate School of Media and Communication (GSMC) Dean, Professor Lawrence Pintak pointed out the role the school is playing to promote quality journalism in the region.

"GSMC looks forward to enhancing its capacity as the premier institution in the region for the development of journalists and media professionals who can tell the stories of this part of the world, and shape the narratives of how these stories interact with the identities and cultures of the people of East Africa. Amidst global upheavals, the journalism industry and higher education have new opportunities to reinvent themselves and we are set to lead the way for East Africa and beyond in wrestling with the questions of our age," added Professor Pintak.

The three teams will be the second cohort since the program launched. The first cohort comprised of Debunk Media and Ludique works, are closing in to their demo days as they edge closer to graduation.
